## 1b. Sample and format parameters for PSA iterations

I'm providing you with functions I've developed & used in prior publications for fitting the pert, beta, and gamma distributions to a provided mean and the 2.5th and 97.5th quantile, then sampling from the distribution. `rpert_mean_quantile` fits and samples from a pert distribution; `rbeta_mean_quantile` fits and samples from a beta distribution, and `rgamma_mean_quantile` fits and samples from a gamma distribution.

```{r sample_distr_functions}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Functions for fitting and sampling from distributions"

rpert_mean_quantile<- function(mean, lb, ub, n=1, adjust_bounds = FALSE){
  mode = (6*mean - lb - ub)/4
  if (adjust_bounds == TRUE){
    if (mode < lb){
      print(paste0(
        "Cannot achieve desired expected value with upper bound of ", ub, "."
      ))
      ub = 6*mean - 5*lb
      mode=lb
      print(paste0(
        "Reset upper bound to ", ub, "."
      ))
    } else if (mode > ub) {
      print(paste0(
        "Cannot achieve desired expected value with lower bound of ", lb, "."
      ))
      lb = 6*mean - 5*ub
      mode=ub
      print(paste0(
        "Reset lower bound to ", lb, "."
      ))
    } 
  } else {
    if (mode < lb){
      mode = lb
      print(paste0("Set mode to lower bound. Mean will be ", (5*lb+ub)/6,
                   "instead of ", mean))
    } else if (mode > ub) {
      mode = ub
      print(paste0("Set mode to lower bound. Mean will be ", (5*ub+lb)/6,
                   "instead of ", mean))
    } 
  }
  return(rpert(n, lb, mode, ub))
}

#Adapted from mc2d R package
#.  https://github.com/cran/mc2d/blob/master/R/pert.R#L159
rpert <- function(n,min=-1,mode=0,max=1,shape=4, mean=0){
  if (length(n) > 1) 
    n <- length(n)
  if (length(n) == 0 || as.integer(n) == 0) 
    return(numeric(0))
  n <- as.integer(n)
  
  if (!missing(mode) && !missing(mean)) stop("specify 'mode' or 'mean' but not both")

  min <- rep(as.vector(min),length.out=n)
  max <- rep(as.vector(max),length.out=n)
  shape <- rep(as.vector(shape),length.out=n)
  
  if (missing(mode)){
    mean <- rep(as.vector(mean),length.out=n)
    mode <- ((shape+2)*mean - min - max) / shape
    if(any(mode < min | mode > max)) warning("Some values of mean lead to mode < min or mode > max.")
    
  } else {  mode <- rep(as.vector(mode),length.out=n) }
  
  a1 <- 1 + shape * (mode - min)/(max - min)
  a2 <- 1 + shape * (max - mode)/(max - min)
  oldw <- options(warn = -1)
  r <- rbeta(n, shape1 = a1, shape2 = a2) * (max - min) + min
  options(warn = oldw$warn)
  minmodemax <- (abs(min - max) < (.Machine$double.eps^0.5))
  r <- ifelse(minmodemax, min, r)
  if (any(is.na(r))) 
    warning("NaN in rpert")
  return(r)
}


# Adapted from prevalence R package
#.  https://github.com/cran/prevalence/blob/master/R/betaExpert.R
betaExpert <-
function(best, lower, upper, p = 0.95, method = "mean"){
  ## check presence
  if (missing(best))
    stop("'best' is missing")
  if (missing(lower) & missing(upper))
    stop("at least 'lower' or 'upper' must be specified")

  ## check input values: order
  if (!missing(lower))
    if (lower > best) stop("'lower' cannot be greater than 'best'")
  if (!missing(upper))
    if (upper < best) stop("'upper' cannot be smaller than 'best'")
  if (!missing(lower) & !missing(upper)) # useless??
    if (lower > upper) stop("'lower' cannot be greater than 'upper'")

  ## functions to optimize ~ mode
  f_mode <-
  function(x, mode, p, target){
    return(
      sum(
        (qbeta(p = p,
               shape1 = x,
               shape2 = (x * (1 - mode) + 2 * mode - 1) / mode) -
         target) ^ 2
    ))
  }

  f_mode_zero <-
  function(x, p, target){
    return((qbeta(p = p, shape1 = 1, shape2 = x) - target) ^ 2)
  }

  f_mode_one <-
  function(x, p, target){
    return((qbeta(p = p, shape1 = x, shape2 = 1) - target) ^ 2)
  }

  ## functions to optimize ~ mean
  f_mean <-
  function(x, mean, p, target){
    return(
      sum(
        (qbeta(p = p,
               shape1 = x,
               shape2 = (x * (1 - mean)) / mean) -
         target) ^ 2
    ))
  }

  ## define 'target' and 'p'
  if (!missing(lower) & missing(upper)){
    target <- lower
    p <- 1 - p
  } else if (!missing(upper) & missing(lower)){
    target <- upper
  } else if (!missing(upper) & !missing(lower)){
    target <- c(lower, upper)
    p <- c(0, p) + (1 - p) / 2
  }

  ## derive a and b (=shape1 and shape2)
  if (method == "mode"){
    if (best == 0){
      a <- 1
      b <- optimize(f_mode_zero, c(0, 1000), p = p, target = target)$minimum
    } else if (best == 1) {
      a <- optimize(f_mode_one, c(0, 1000), p = p, target = target)$minimum
      b <- 1
    } else {
      a <- optimize(f_mode, c(0, 1000),
                    mode = best, p = p, target = target)$minimum
      b <- (a * (1 - best) + 2 * best - 1) / best
    }
  } else if (method == "mean"){
      a <- optimize(f_mean, c(0, 1000),
                    mean = best, p = p, target = target)$minimum
      b <- (a * (1 - best)) / best
  }

  ## create 'out' dataframe
  out <- list(alpha = a, beta = b)
  class(out) <- "betaExpert"

  ## return 'out'
  return(out)
}

rbeta_mean_quantile <- function(mean, lb, ub, n=1){
  params <- betaExpert(mean, lb, ub)
  return(rbeta(n=n, params$alpha, params$beta))
}

gammaExpert <- function(best, lower, upper, p = 0.95, method = "mean"){
    ## check presence
    if (missing(best))
      stop("'best' is missing")
    if (missing(lower) & missing(upper))
      stop("at least 'lower' or 'upper' must be specified")
    
    ## check input values: order
    if (!missing(lower))
      if (lower > best) stop("'lower' cannot be greater than 'best'")
    if (!missing(upper))
      if (upper < best) stop("'upper' cannot be smaller than 'best'")
    if (!missing(lower) & !missing(upper)) # useless??
      if (lower > upper) stop("'lower' cannot be greater than 'upper'")
    
    
    f_mean <-
      function(x, mean, p, target){
        return(
          sum(
            (qgamma(p = p,
                    shape = x,
                    scale = mean/x) -
               target) ^ 2
          ))
      }
    
    ## define 'target' and 'p'
    if (!missing(lower) & missing(upper)){
      target <- lower
      p <- 1 - p
    } else if (!missing(upper) & missing(lower)){
      target <- upper
    } else if (!missing(upper) & !missing(lower)){
      target <- c(lower, upper)
      p <- c(0, p) + (1 - p) / 2
    }
    
    ## derive a and b (=shape1 and shape2)
    
    if (method == "mean"){
      a <- optimize(f_mean, c(0, 1000),
                    mean = best, p = p, target = target)$minimum #a is shape parameter
      b <- best / a #b is scale parameter
    }
    
    ## create 'out' dataframe
    out <- list(shape = a, scale = b)
    #class(out) <- "betaExpert"
    
    ## return 'out'
    return(out)
}

rgamma_mean_quantile <- function(mean, lb, ub, n=1){
  params <- gammaExpert(mean, lb, ub)
  return(rgamma(n=n, shape=params$shape, scale=params$scale))
}
```

# 2. Differential equation model

This section is uses the model of a hypothetical sexually transmitted disease (loosely based on HIV) from [Menzies et. al. 2017](https://doi.org/10.1007/s40273-017-0494-4), a tutorial on Bayesian model calibration. They provide working [R code for their implementation of model](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/QXM09F).

The model states and parameters for this model are defined in this figure:

![](menzies_model.png)

The differential equations defining this model are:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{dN}{dt} &= ab - \mu^{B} N & \text{non-susceptible} \\
\frac{dS}{dt} &= a(1-b) - \mu^{B} S - \lambda_tS & \text{susceptible} \\
\frac{dE}{dt} &= \lambda_tS - (\mu^{B} + \mu^{E}) E - r_t^E E - cE & \text{early disease} \\
\frac{dL}{dt} &= pE - (\mu^{B} + \mu^{L}) L - r^L L & \text{late disease} \\
\frac{dT}{dt} &= r_t^E E + r^L L - (\mu^{B} + \mu^{T}) T & \text{on treatment} \\
\frac{dD}{dt} &= \mu^{B} (N+S+E+L+T) + \mu^{E} E + \mu^{L} L + \mu^{T} T & \text{dead}
\end{aligned}
$$

The force of infection $\lambda_t$ is defined as $\lambda_t = \rho \frac{E+L}{S+E+L+T}$, where $\rho$ is the effective contact rate. The model simulation begins at time 0 (corresponding to 1990) until time 51 (corresponding to 2040). Years 0-30 (1990-2020) are used to simulate the epidemic until the "present day," and years 30-51 (2020-2040) are used to project future outcomes for a policy comparison. The policy comparison is between two scenarios:

-   **Base case:** only individuals with late-stage disease initiate treatment
-   **Expanded treatment:** individuals with early-stage disease initiate treatment at the same rate beginning in year 30.

The rate of treatment update during early disease $r^E$ is set to 0 for the first 30 years in both scenarios. In the "expanded treatment access" scenario, $r^E$ is set to the same value as $r^L$ beginning in year 30.

## 1a. Menzies 2019 implementation

This code chunk shows the model implementation from Menzies et. al. with minor edits.

```{r}
##############################################
################### MODEL ####################
##############################################
# This function estimates outcomes describing epidemiology of a hypothetical disease
# to assess a policy that expands treatment access to individual's with early 
# stage disease.

mod_menzies <- function(par_vector, init_pop) {
  # par_vector: a vector of model parameters
  mu_e    <- par_vector[1]   # cause-specific mortality rate with early-stage disease
  mu_l    <- par_vector[2]   # cause-specific mortality rate with late-stage disease
  mu_t    <- par_vector[3]   # cause-specific mortality rate on treatment
  p       <- par_vector[4]   # transtion rate from early to late-stage disease
  r_l    <- par_vector[5]   # rate of uptake onto treatment from late-stage disease
  r_e    <- par_vector[6]   # rate of uptake onto treatment from early-stage disease (only non-zero in expanded treatment access scenario)
  rho    <- par_vector[7]   # effective contact rate 
  b      <- par_vector[8]   # fraction of population in at-risk group
  mu_b   <- par_vector[9]  # background mortality rate
  a      <- par_vector[10] # annual birth rate   
  
  ######## Prepare to run model ###################
  n_yrs    <- 51   # no. years to simulate (30 to present, 51 for 20 year analytic horizon)
  sim      <- 1:2  # which scenarios to simulate: 1 = base case, 2 = expanded treatment access
  v_mu     <- c(0,0,mu_e,mu_l,mu_t)+mu_b             # vector of mortality rates
  trace    <- matrix(NA,12*n_yrs+1,6)                  # creates a table to store simulation trace
  colnames(trace) <- c("N","S","E","L","T","D")
  rownames(trace) <- seq(from=0, to=51, by=1/12)
  results  <- list("base_case" = trace,
                   "expanded_tx" = trace)
  
  ######## Run model ###################
  for(s in sim) { # loop over two scenarios: 1 = base case, 2 = expanded treatment access
    # reset population vector to initial population at start of simulation
    #.   and fill in first row of trace matrix (cohort distribution across states
    #.   at time 0)
    results[[s]][1,] <- P0 <- P1 <- init_pop 
    
    # loop over months and update state distribution
    for(m in 1:(12*n_yrs)) { 
      # P0: population distribution at start of month
      # P!: population distribution at end of month (after applying transitions)
      
      # calculate force of infection
      lambda    <- rho*sum(P0[3:4])/sum(P0[2:5]) 
      
      # calculate transitions each month and update P1
      #.  births: entries into N and S
      P1[1]   <- P1[1]+a*(1-b)/12 
      P1[2]   <- P1[2]+a*b/12
      #.  deaths: N, S, E, L, T, to D
      P1[-6]    <- P1[-6]-P0[-6]*v_mu/12         
      P1[6]     <- P1[6]+sum(P0[-6]*v_mu/12)
      #.  infections: S to E
      P1[2]     <- P1[2]-P0[2]*lambda/12         
      P1[3]     <- P1[3]+P0[2]*lambda/12
      #.  disease progression: E to L
      P1[3]     <- P1[3]-P0[3]*p/12
      P1[4]     <- P1[4]+P0[3]*p/12
      #.  treatment uptake: L to T
      P1[4]     <- P1[4]-P0[4]*r_l/12
      P1[5]     <- P1[5]+P0[4]*r_l/12
      
      if(s==2 & m>(12*30)) {
        #.  treatment uptake: E to T (scenario 2)
        P1[3]   <- P1[3]-P0[3]*r_e/12
        P1[5]   <- P1[5]+P0[3]*r_e/12
      }
      results[[s]][m+1,] <- P0 <- P1                      # fill trace, reset pop vectors
    }
  }
  
  ######## Report results ###################
  return(results)
}


# create vector of parameters

)

        year=as.numeric(rownames(trace_base_case)),
        scenario="base case"),
  cbind(as.data.frame(trace_expanded_tx),
        year=as.numeric(rownames(trace_base_case)),
        scenario="expanded tx")
) |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = c("N","S","E","L","T","D"), names_to = "state", values_to = "count")


ggplot(data = t_trace_long) +
  geom_line(aes(x=year, y=count, color=state))+
  facet_wrap(~scenario)+
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma)+
  labs(x="Year", y="Number of people", color="Health state")+
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")+
  geom_vline(xintercept = 30, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey")+
  ggtitle("Cohort trace, all cohorts and all years")

# Plot from year 30 on, excluding the non-susceptible and dead cohorts
ggplot(data = t_trace_long |> filter(year >= 30, !state %in% c("N","D"))) +
  geom_line(aes(x=year, y=count, color=state))+
  facet_wrap(~scenario)+
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma)+
  labs(x="Year", y="Number of people", color="Health state")+
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")+
  geom_vline(xintercept = 30, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey")+
  ggtitle("Cohort trace, years 30-51")

```

## 1b. Implementing with desolve

```{r}
deq_system = function(
                      times, #time points to evaluate 
                      y, # state variables at t[1] (usually 0)
                      parms #parameter vector
                      ){
  
  
  # Extract parameters from parms vector
  mu_e  <- parms[1]   # cause-specific mortality rate with early-stage disease
  mu_l <- parms[2]   # cause-specific mortality rate with late-stage disease
  mu_t <- parms[3]   # cause-specific mortality rate on treatment
  p    <- parms[4]   # transtion rate from early to late-stage disease
  r_l  <- parms[5]   # rate of uptake onto treatment from late-stage disease
  r_e  <- parms[6]   # rate of uptake onto treatment from early-stage disease (only non-zero in expanded treatment access scenario)
  rho  <- parms[7]   # effective contact rate 
  b    <- parms[8]   # fraction of population in at-risk group
  mu_b <- parms[9]           # background mortality rate hard-coded as 0.015
  
  
  # Extract state variables from y
  N <- y[1]
  S <- y[2]
  E <- y[3]
  L <- y[4]
  T <- y[5]
  D <- y[6]
  
  # Calculate force of infection
  lambdat   <- rho*(E+L)/(S+E+L+T)
  
  # Define differential equations
  dN_dt = mu_b*b - mu_b*N #dN/dt
  dS_dt = mu_b*(1-b) - mu_b*S - lambdat*S #dS/dt
  dE_dt = lambdat*S - (mu_b + mu_e)*E - r_e*E - p*E #dE/dt
  dL_dt = p*E - (mu_b + mu_l)*L - r_l*L #dL/dt
  dT_dt = r_e*E + r_l*L - (mu_b + mu_t)*T #dT/dt
  dD_dt = mu_b*(N+S+E+L+T) + mu_e*E + mu_l*L + mu_t*T #dD/dt
  
  # Return list of derivatives
  return(
    c("N" = dN_dt, "S" = dS_dt, "E" = dE_dt, 
      "L" = dL_dt, "T" = dT_dt, "T" = dD_dt) |>list()
  )
}
```

```{r}
                0.25, #mu_L

                0.5, #rho
                0.20) #b
```
